title: SXSW Dispatch: Breaking News--This Newsletter Files Complaint About Self-same Complaint
subtitle: An imagined absurdist future, as a commentary of recursive stupidity in generative AI
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE DISTRICT OF Austin, Texas.

COMPLAINT FOR INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INFRINGEMENT

Plaintiff, the Frontier Psychiatrists newsletter (tFPn), by and through its undersigned counsel, hereby brings this Complaint against itself for willful infringement of its own intellectual property rights in violation of the Copyright Act of 1976, as amended, 17 U.S.C. §§ 101 et seq.

PARTIES

• Plaintiff, tFPn, is a legal entity duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of New York, with its principal place of business located at Williamsburg, Brooklyn, somewhere between N 8th and N 9th streets. Plaintiff is the owner of all intellectual property rights in and to the written work set forth in the Complaint.

• Defendant, tFPn, is a legal entity duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of New York, with its principal place of business located at Williamsburg, Brooklyn, somewhere between N 8th and N 9th streets—keep going, you will see it! Defendant is also the owner of all intellectual property rights in and to the written work set forth in the Complaint.

JURISDICTION AND VENUE

• This Court has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331 and 1338, as the matter arises under the Copyright Act of 1976, as amended.

• Venue is proper in this judicial district pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b), as Plaintiff and Defendant are believed to be operating within this district, and a substantial part of the events giving rise to the claim occurred within this district. Given they are the same entity, the venue is likely to be the least of the issues raised in this matter, honestly.

FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS

• Plaintiff and Defendant are the owners of all intellectual property rights in and to this written work, in the form of this very article about this complaint right now, include these words, the preceding and subsequent words and phrases, as set forth in the Complaint, which is itself the thing about which the complaint is filed.

• Plaintiff has copied and reproduced the Complaint in its entirety without consent or authorization from the original author, thereby infringing on the intellectual property rights of the original author in the process of its authorship.

• Plaintiff's infringement of the intellectual property rights of the original authors has been willful, intentional, and malicious. Despite having actual or constructive knowledge of the exclusive rights owned by the original authors, Plaintiff has nonetheless continued to infringe on those rights in disregard of the rights of the original authors. This defendant is a real Piece of work, including this extremely biased statement itself.

• Plaintiff's actions have caused the original authors to suffer irreparable harm, including but not limited to a loss of revenue and reputation, as well as other economic damages, including the very authorial time spent drafting this very complaint, which adds insult to injury.

• On account of the egregious nature of the manifestly true nature of the recursive complaint, Plaintiff asks for punitive damages to be levied in addition to any any all compensation awarded by the court.

COUNT ONE - COPYRIGHT INFRINGEMENT

• Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference the allegations contained in paragraphs 1-8 above.

• Plaintiff's unauthorized copying and reproduction of the Complaint constitutes copyright infringement in violation of the Copyright Act of 1976, as amended.

• Plaintiff is liable as the original author for damages in an amount to be determined at trial, but in no event less than the statutory minimum, and honeslty, a lot more than usual.

PRAYER FOR RELIEF

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter judgment against Plaintiff as follows:

A. A finding that Plaintiff has infringed on the intellectual property rights of the original authors in violation of the Copyright Act of 1976, as amended;

B. An award of damages in an amount to be determined at trial, but in no event less than the statutory minimum;

C. An award of the original authors' costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys' fees incurred in connection with this action; and

D. An injunction prohibiting Plaintiff from further infringing on the intellectual property rights of the original authors. Seriously.

JURY DEMAND

Plaintiff demands a trial by jury on all issues so triable.

Respectfully submitted,

—Owen Scott Muir, M.D.,

Representing self as both Plaintiff and Defendant.

Thank you for reading The Frontier Psychiatrists . This post is public but not covered under Creative Commons, so feel free to letter bomb this to enemies and use it in discovery to prove intent about your absurdist IP lawsuit.
